preserveMtime.result: writes to an already-closed transcript preserve its mtime
preserveMtime.note: File-date signal stays with the last real event. ls -lt, retention, and recent-session pickers keep the days work actually happened.

timestampRequired.result: any appended record carries a timestamp, so the write is auditable from content
timestampRequired.note: last-prompt and mode currently carry no timestamp field. Content's last real event can be days or weeks earlier while mtime moves.

shadow.result: min 3 days, median 17 days, max 47 days; 93 of 114 more than 7 days after last real event

hypothesis.status: labeled observation, not a proven trigger
observables: many long-closed transcripts were appended to in one bulk operation
the appended records are timestamp-free metadata types
mtime moved and content did not

point: A shared mtime is not a hold. Score the gnomon or admit cast. Same-class #90932 is a display stitch (data intact on disk). #90955 is version-signal skew, not mtime.
